A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain corresponding material, including Appendices A–J. Full text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables, and proofs.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of image deblurring, Navier–Stokes prediction, linear programming, and looped-transformer outputs in Section 3, with additional model-scaling experiments in Appendices G–H.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 3 and Appendices G–H, including quantitative comparisons and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The PGD/HQS, FNO, GNN, and looped-transformer formulations are unchanged. Their components, training strategies, and inference procedures match across Section 3 and Appendices B and F–I.

E1.justification: Both versions use BSDS500 deblurring, steady Navier–Stokes data, generated linear programs, and the same 200 semantic-contrast prompt pairs. The perturbed-input test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same explicit DRUNet, FNO, and GNN comparators, including the deeper and wider explicit variants in Tables 3–6. No comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, perturbation procedures, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and inference iteration counts are identical in Section 3 and Appendices G–I.

E4.justification: The iteration-wise expressivity and accuracy analyses, input-perturbation tests, explicit-model scaling comparisons, and language case study are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same mean and standard-deviation reporting over evaluated samples. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or statistical-testing information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 4 retains 29.18 dB for implicit HQS, and Tables 5–6 retain 0.0785 relative error for implicit FNO; the language outputs in Table 2 are also identical.

T1.justification: The regular-operator definition, assumptions, sufficiency and necessity theorems, application-specific mathematical results, and derivations and proofs in Appendices A–E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion make identical expressivity and test-time scaling claims. The new title's reference to rich equilibria restates the existing claim about the richness of fixed-point maps.

C2.justification: Interpretations of increasing Lipschitz estimates and generalization are unchanged. Both retain the difficulty of formally extending the theory to language tokens in Section 3.4 and the lack of enforced regularity discussed in Appendix F.

D1.justification: Appendices F–I retain identical implementation, hyperparameter, preprocessing, training, and hardware disclosures. The semantic-contrast dataset access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Citations and research positioning are identical, including Appendix J's discussions of prior expressivity, convergence, generalization, and kernel analyses.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Implicit Models: Expressive Power Scales with Test-Time Compute' to 'Expressive Power of Implicit Models: Rich Equilibria and Test-Time Scaling'. Running headers and date/version text are updated; body prose and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–6 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement. Page arrangements remain the same; the title and running-header wording edits are recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: v3 retitles the paper and updates headers and dates while preserving the scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, reproducibility information, and limitations. These editorial changes do not materially alter the paper's clarity, completeness, or evidential support.
